title: Ferrari Obstacle Drift Challenge
description: A top-down drift racing game where the player steers a Ferrari through a procedurally arranged obstacle course of ShaderBalls. The player must navigate between rows of ShaderBalls, collecting glowing checkpoints while avoiding collisions, with speed increasing over time and a scoring system tracking distance and pickups.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 that implements a Ferrari obstacle drift challenge game. Load ferrari.glb as the player-controlled car and ShaderBall.glb as obstacles. Setup: Use a third-person chase camera positioned behind and above the Ferrari, looking down at roughly 35 degrees. Add a ground plane with a dark asphalt-textured grid material. Place directional light plus ambient light for clear visibility. Spawn ShaderBalls in staggered rows of 3-5 across the road at regular Z intervals, each scaled to roughly match the car size. ShaderBalls should have a subtle emissive glow using MeshStandardMaterial override with emissive color. Game mechanics: The Ferrari drives forward automatically at increasing speed (starting at 15 units/sec, increasing by 0.5 every 5 seconds, capped at 40). The player steers left/right using arrow keys or A/D keys with smooth interpolation and drift physics (apply lateral velocity decay of 0.92 per frame). Implement collision detection using bounding boxes between the Ferrari and each ShaderBall. On collision, flash the screen red, deduct one of three lives displayed as heart icons in an HTML overlay HUD, and briefly make the car invincible for 1.5 seconds with a blinking effect. Place golden checkpoint rings (simple torus geometry) between some ShaderBall rows. Driving through a checkpoint adds 100 points with a particle burst effect using BufferGeometry points. The HUD must display: current score, current speed, lives remaining, and distance traveled. Recycle obstacles and checkpoints by repositioning them ahead when they pass behind the camera. Implement a start screen overlay with a Play button, and a game-over screen showing final score with a Restart button. Add subtle fog for depth. Validate that speed increases correctly, lives decrement on collision, score increments on checkpoint collection, and game ends at zero lives. All interaction must use keyboard input with visual feedback for each state change.
